label: S. 1096

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Preserve Access to Affordable Generics and Biosimilars Act prohibits brand-name drug and biological product manufacturers from entering into settlement agreements with generic or biosimilar manufacturers that include compensation and restrict the development, manufacturing, or sale of generic or biosimilar products. These agreements are presumed to have anticompetitive effects unless specific exemptions apply. The Federal Trade Commission is given enforcement authority, and violators face civil penalties and potential forfeiture of marketing exclusivity periods.

affected_groups.effect: Prohibited from providing certain types of compensation to generic or biosimilar competitors in exchange for delaying product market entry and subject to civil penalties and FTC enforcement for violations.
affected_groups.group: Brand-name drug and biological product manufacturers

affected_groups.effect: Prohibited from accepting compensation to delay market entry, subject to forfeiture of the 180-day marketing exclusivity period if found in violation, and required to comply with strict agreement certification rules.
affected_groups.group: Generic drug and biosimilar application filers

affected_groups.effect: Granted specific oversight, investigation, enforcement, and litigation authorities to penalize prohibited anticompetitive settlement agreements.
affected_groups.group: Federal Trade Commission and Department of Justice

key_provisions: Prohibits agreements resolving patent claims between brand-name and generic or biosimilar drug manufacturers that have anticompetitive effects.
Presumes agreements are anticompetitive if a generic or biosimilar applicant receives anything of value and agrees to limit or forgo research, development, manufacturing, marketing, or sales.

Provides specific exemptions for settlements where the only consideration received by the generic or biosimilar filer is the right to market prior to patent expiration, reasonable litigation expenses, or a covenant not to sue.
Authorizes the Federal Trade Commission to bring civil actions and seek civil penalties, which cannot exceed three times the value received reasonably attributable to the violation.

Requires company executives to certify that filings submitted to the FTC and Department of Justice concerning drug agreements represent the complete and exclusive agreement between parties, including oral understandings.
missing_information: Specific details regarding the exact number of individuals or total market revenue that will be directly altered outside of general congressional findings on overall industry spending.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Preserve Access to Affordable Generics and Biosimilars Act prohibits brand-name drug and biological product manufacturers from entering into settlement agreements with generic or biosimilar manufacturers that include compensation and restrict the development, manufacturing, or sale of generic or biosimilar products. These agreements are presumed to have anticompetitive effects unless specific exemptions apply. The Federal Trade Commission is given enforcement authority, and violators face civil penalties and potential forfeiture of marketing exclusivity periods.
summary_detail.significance: This bill addresses business practices in the pharmaceutical industry by targeting patent settlement agreements that involve payments tied to delayed generic or biosimilar market entry. By establishing statutory presumptions and penalties enforced by the FTC, the legislation alters how brand-name and generic drug manufacturers can resolve patent disputes.

title: Preserve Access to Affordable Generics and Biosimilars Act
